approvedDesign.title: Turncoat A: the ward turns hostile when it has covered half of its walk to the exit and no squad member is in a fight; the terms change to killing it
approvedDesign.problem: Turncoat rolls on escort, rescue, retrieval and siege (missiontypes.js:833, weight 5, x1.5) and nothing reads it. Only escort and rescue have a person on the paper, the ward, and the ward is inert: it has no species, so fighterFor returns null for it (sortie.js:133), a fight with it alone on one side is cancelled and both sides get noFightUntil + 120 (sortie.js:159-161), and FAIL.died("ward") cannot fire (0 of 960 baseline escort and rescue contracts ended with a dead ward). Escort has the lowest death rate of the 15 types at levels 1-4 (0.02 per contract over 1800 contracts on the real harness; 0.33 at levels 1-8 over 240), so the tag costs nothing today on the contract that would feel it most. The first version of this proposal turned the ward at the first fight within 3 tiles of it. Measured on the real harness that trigger turned the ward in only 29% (levels 1-4) and 36% (levels 1-8) of contracts, and in 78% and 88% of those the turn was the first fight of the run, so the squad had no earlier fight to prepare for.
evidence: missiontypes.js:833-834 turncoat row; the id appears in no other .js file. missiontypes.js:414 and :599 set `frail: true` on the ward cast lines; grep finds no reader.

sortie.js:133 (`if (!a.species) return null`) and sortie.js:159-161 (`nobody to fight on one side` sets noFightUntil = clock + 120 for everyone in the skirmish): the ward is never hurt and a hostile that reaches it alone is pacified for 120 s.

field.js:1186-1196 combatant(): a ward is a combatant only when no squad actor is within 1 tile; field.js:739-745 guard orders keep the squad within GUARD_LEASH = 2 (:49) of the ward; field.js:758-764 the ward walks to the exit once it is free.
field.js:1562-1580 escalate() already rewrites m.win and m.lose during a run, and field.js:2018 save() stores `mission: s.mission` whole, so a rewritten win list survives a reload.

field.js:1687-1717 makeActor builds species, label, icon, hp, power, speed and wits from a grade and the injected namer; start() keeps that namer as s.name (:2072), so a turn can call `s.name({ role: "hostile", grade }, s.mission)`.

missions.js BESTIARY, checked with the namer's own filter (fieldview.js namer): the only elite-tier species tagged for the escort theme (humanoid, beast, goblin) or the rescue theme (humanoid, goblin, undead) is the Death Knight (dex 10); veteran-tier turns (Wolf, Slime Soldier) measured no effect earlier (0.49 vs 0.50 deaths per contract).
field.js:1519 rawWin: `eliminate` is met when every actor named "ward" is dead; matches() (:98) tests a.name, so a ward that keeps name "ward" and changes role stays addressable by the new atom.
field.js:1477 contacted() reads `a.spotted` of any actor: a traitor created with spotted = true ends the free call-off at the turn.

Measured with test/sortie.harness.js on a scratch copy of the project (snapshot 03:42; later field.js/sortie.js changes add only the contacted/retreat plumbing): escort and rescue only, twist pinned, gearless squads of 4 from a 24-character pool (3-5 stars), 3 seeds x 160 contracts per level band. approvedDesign.change:
MODS (missiontypes.js:833, on top of u-honesty): turncoat: { label: "Turncoat", weight: 8, reward: 1.35, only: ["escort", "rescue"], trial: false, mods: { turn: { progress: 0.5, grade: "elite", levelOffset: -4 } } }. `only` narrows from four types to two (retrieval and siege have no person on the paper). Weight is 8 because two types instead of four halve the eligible contracts: weight 5 over four types was 0.84% of all contracts at level 10, weight 8 over two types is 0.67% and weight 10 would restore 0.84%.
MOD_TEXT.turn(mods, mission): "The ward turns hostile when it has covered 50% of its walk to the exit (rescue: counted from when it is freed) and no squad member is in a fight. It becomes an elite-tier fighter, level N (the contract level minus 3). The terms then read: Kill the ward + Everyone still standing gets out. Before it turns the ward cannot fight or be hurt."

CONSUMERS.
1) field.js turn(s, w), new, beside escalate() (:1562). Names a species with `s.name({ role: "hostile", grade: mods.turn.grade }, s.mission)` and sets: side "theirs", role "hostile", grade, levelOffset, species, label (the species label; name stays "ward" so atoms that name the ward still find it), icon, sprite, hp = maxHp = GRADE_HP[grade], power = GRADE_POWER[grade], speed = BASE_SPEED x speedOf(named), wits from the species attrs (the same lines as makeActor), spotted = true, captive = false. It rewrites the terms the way escalate() does: m.win drops every atom with who "ward" (extract, protect) and gains OBJ.eliminate("ward") in front; m.lose drops FAIL.died("ward"). s.counters.turned = s.clock and one log line: "The ward is now hostile: Death Knight, elite tier, level 7. Terms: Kill the ward + Everyone still standing gets out."
2) field.js step() (:2117), after arrivals and before chooseGoals: the ward is the first actor with role "ward" that is alive, not extracted and not (captive and not freed). On the first step it can move, w.d0 = its distance to the exit field (fieldTo(s, "exit", [portalPoint(s)]), already built every step for the ward's own goal). When counters.turned is unset, 1 - d / w.d0 >= mods.turn.progress and no squad actor is engaged, call turn(s, w). Rescue measures from the step after the ward is freed (field.js:760), escort from the first step.
3) No contact trigger: openSkirmish is not changed. A retreat order does not stop the turn (the ward walks to the same exit the retreat uses).
4) field.js kill() (:1255): a dead actor named "ward" with counters.turned set logs "the turncoat is dead" instead of falling through silently (its role is no longer "ward").
5) field.js ACTOR_KEYS (:1970) + "d0"; counters.turned rides with counters. Role, side, grade, species, hp, maxHp, power, speed, wits and levelOffset are already in ACTOR_KEYS; fieldview.js rehydrate() restores the sprite from species after a reload.
6) sortie.js fighterFor (:133-137) needs no change: it builds the traitor at mission.level + GRADE_BUMP.elite (1) + levelOffset (-4) = level - 3, minimum 1. The Death Knight is the only species the namer can return for these themes.
7) missiontypes.js: row, MOD_TEXT.turn; delete `frail: true` from the two ward cast lines (:414, :599). Decision on `frail`: it has no reader today and this change does not give it one. An unturned ward stays a non-combatant that takes no damage; making wards killable would move the death rate of every escort and rescue, not only Turncoat's, and is a separate proposal.
8) Requires pursuit-twist-plumbing for the trial filter (`trial: false`). No spawn hook is used.
9) test/contracts.js: a rescue ward does not turn and sets no d0 before it is freed; an escort ward turns once at 50% progress and not while a squad actor is engaged (it turns on the first step none is); after the turn the win list has eliminate("ward") first and no atom with who "ward" besides it, the lose list has no died("ward"), objectiveText renders "Kill the ward"; save/restore after the turn keeps role, side, species, d0 and counters.turned and the traitor fights as a Death Knight at level - 3; a squad that kills the traitor and extracts wins with the attrition resolver; a retreat order before the turn does not prevent it; rollTwists never returns turncoat for retrieval or siege; the ward cast lines have no `frail`.

CARD. Tag "Turncoat" titled with MOD_TEXT.turn. The listed terms (extract the ward, keep it alive) are the client's and stay on the card; the tooltip says what they become. MAP. The ward's gold disc becomes the Death Knight sprite at the turn (fieldview.js:213-224 draws side "theirs" as a sprite); the run panel objective list re-renders from m.win and m.lose, so the new terms show as unmet.

MEASURED (escort + rescue, 3 seeds x 160 contracts per band, same seeds in every arm). Levels 1-4: win 81.7% -> 76.0%; deaths per contract 0.106 -> 0.202 (+90%; per seed +0.14, +0.03, +0.12); escort 0.02 -> 0.09, rescue 0.19 -> 0.31. Levels 1-8: win 66.0% -> 60.0%; deaths 0.415 -> 0.654 (+58%; per seed +0.36, +0.10, +0.26); escort 0.33 -> 0.73 (94% -> 87% wins), rescue 0.50 -> 0.57 (38% -> 33%). The escort ward turns in every contract (240 of 240 at both bands); the rescue ward turns in 58% (levels 1-4) and 35% (levels 1-8) of contracts, and every other rescue ended before the ward had walked half: the squad lost a fight or withdrew first (all 101 and 155 contracts without a turn are rescue). Among turned contracts 55% (levels 1-4) and 50% (levels 1-8) turn before any fight has opened, and the mean is 2.0 fights before the turn, so in about half the contracts the traitor is the first fight, not a second act. Progress dial, levels 1-8: 35% gives +45% deaths, 50% gives +58%, 65% gives +79%. Contact trigger (first version): +73% and +82% but it fires in 29% and 36% of contracts.

MULTIPLIER x1.35 (was x1.5). Rule: the multiplier R that leaves the expected gems per contract unchanged, R = (P0 + (d1 - d0) x C) / P1, where P is the mean pay actually earned per contract (a win earns W0 = (25 + 30 x level) x type multiplier, a loss earns 0), d is deaths per contract, and C = 100 gems is the summon price (game.js:8 PULL_COST), so a death costs one replacement pull. Levels 1-8: P0/P1 = 1.138 and (d1 - d0) x C / P1 = (0.654 - 0.415) x 100 / P1 = 0.185, R = 1.323, rounded up to the next 0.05 = 1.35. Levels 1-4: 1.086 + 0.079 = 1.165. If a death is valued at 200 gems the same data give 1.51 (levels 1-8) and 1.24 (levels 1-4). A flat x1.35 overpays by about 0.2 at levels 1-4; making the multiplier a function of level belongs in MT.factors for every twist, not in this row. A player can check the inputs on screen: the base pay on the card, the price on the Summon button, the tag's multiplier, the turn log line (species, tier, level) and afterwards the debrief line.

FREQUENCY weight 8 (was 5), only [escort, rescue], trial false. Under the u-honesty draw rule (chance = odds x weight / 66, odds 0.2 to 0.6 by level): 2.5 / 3.7 / 5.4 / 8.7% of escort and rescue contracts at levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20, 0.31 / 0.47 / 0.67 / 1.09% of all contracts; at least one on a 5-contract board 1.5 / 2.3 / 3.3 / 5.3%. With all nine rows live the cap binds (pool weight above 66) and the figures are 2.0 / 3.1 / 4.5 / 7.6% of escort and rescue. Weight 5 gives 0.20 / 0.29 / 0.42 / 0.68% of all contracts.
approvedDesign.playerEffect: Before launch the card says the ward becomes an elite-tier fighter at half its walk, so the decision is whether this squad can kill a level-(contract - 3) elite that starts inside its own ranks: burst, a tank, healing, potions. It makes escort the first low-risk contract with a real death rate (0.02 -> 0.09 deaths per contract at levels 1-4). During the run the player sees the token change, the log line and the new terms, and can order a retreat, but the order does not prevent the turn: it is keyed to the ward's progress and the ward walks to the same exit the retreat uses. Measured with a crude player that orders a retreat when the squad averages under 60% HP between fights: deaths 0.654 -> 0.583 (-11%) at levels 1-8 and 0.202 -> 0.179 at levels 1-4; of 82 orders at levels 1-8, 61 came after the turn and 21 before it. The same policy without the twist changes deaths by -5% (0.415 -> 0.394). The lever is therefore small; the multiplier prices the full effect.
approvedDesign.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat as built: sortie.js exitState, field.js contacted/retreat): the turn sets spotted on the traitor, so a squad that had no contact yet loses its free call-off at the turn (field.js:1477); the order exists from first contact in escort and does not stop the turn. Wounds (u-wounds): survivors whose lowest HP fell under 0.4 (nadir) 16.3% -> 19.7% at levels 1-8, 11.1% -> 11.1% at levels 1-4. Permanent death: +0.24 deaths per contract at levels 1-8, +0.10 at levels 1-4; 123 of the 314 deaths at levels 1-8 happen before the turn (baseline total 199), 191 after it. Payout: sortie.js settle uses m.reward unchanged and a dead traitor satisfies eliminate("ward"), so a win pays as an escort at x1.35. Bestiary: the Death Knight is recorded when the traitor fights (Bestiary.record in sortie.js resolve), so the town learns the species from the first Turncoat contract. Debrief (u-debrief): one line "Turncoat: the ward turned at M:SS after N fights" from counters.turned and counters.fights.
approvedDesign.risks: The traitor is always a Death Knight: it is the only elite species for both themes, so a bestiary entry added later changes the calibration. The strength is one dial: veteran tier measured nothing earlier, elite at -4 gives the figures above, elite at 0 gave +200% in an earlier runner. In about half the turned contracts the turn is the first fight, so "second act" is not guaranteed. Escort deaths rise 121% at levels 1-8, which turns the safest type into a contract with a real death rate; that is the intent but it is a large change for early squads. The multiplier is flat while the rule gives 1.165 at levels 1-4 and 1.32 at levels 1-8. The loadout plan (sortie.js:112) is built without the traitor species because it is named at the turn. Unturned wards stay invulnerable (see consumer 7). In rescue a squad that never frees the ward never sees a turn. d0 reads the exit distance field; escort and rescue are not standfast, so the exit does not move. Needs u-honesty and pursuit-twist-plumbing first. Figures are from gearless squads; absolute deaths are upper bounds and only the relative change is usable.
approvedDesign.response: Design attack, accepted: the turn at first contact is gone. The trigger is the ward's progress, re-measured above (+58% deaths at levels 1-8 against +82% for the contact trigger, and it fires in every escort and in 35-58% of rescues, 68-79% of contracts overall, instead of 29-36%). Accepted with a measured correction: the turn is still the first fight in about half of the turned contracts. Weight: kept the upper end of the engineering range (8, not 5) because narrowing from four types to two halves the eligible contracts; the weight is one constant and the figures for 5 are given. Accepted: the log line gives species, tier and level instead of a sentence about the ward not being what the contract said. `frail`: decided, see consumer 7. The one-sided-fight quirk (sortie.js:159-161) is why wards are invulnerable; it is documented here and not changed. Engineering attack, accepted: price by level band (both bands are given, with the rule and its inputs), mechanism stated plainly in MOD_TEXT, trial threading moved to pursuit-twist-plumbing, sequencing after u-honesty and u-retreat. Declined: making the multiplier a function of level inside this row; it belongs in MT.factors for all twists. Retrieval and siege leave the row; Turncoat B (the informant) is dropped.

verdicts.attack: The turn lands at the first fight beside the ward, which is first contact, the same second the free call-off ends under u-retreat: an elite Death Knight appears inside the squad's ranks in its first fight with no reaction window and nothing the player decides during the run. +63% deaths at levels 1-8 (0.371 to 0.606) on the two safest contract types, and the weight hike 5 to 12 puts it on one escort or rescue in eight at level 20. The pre-launch decision is a difficulty gate (can this squad kill a level-3 elite); a squad that can does so on any escort. The traitor is always a Death Knight because it is the only elite species with humanoid or undead tags, so a merchant becomes a Death Knight on every Turncoat contract. Unturned wards stay invulnerable and frail (missiontypes.js:414, 599) stays unread.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: TWISTS.turncoat missiontypes.js:833 (weight 5, x1.5, four types); ward has no species so fighterFor returns null (sortie.js:133) and resolve's one-sided fight cancels with noFightUntil +120 (:158-160); combatant() ward rule field.js:1185-1195; escalate() rewrites and saves :1537-1561; ward goal exit :757-764, GUARD_LEASH 2 :49; makeActor :1662-1688; ACTOR_KEYS has role/side/grade/species/hp/power/speed/wits/levelOffset :1943; escort and rescue are deadline true so exitFor gives 'window' (:192-196, :409, :595); elite bestiary entries missions.js:51-56: three slimes, stone golem, death_knight, the last the only one tagged humanoid/undead, matching escort (humanoid, beast, goblin) and rescue (humanoid, goblin, undead) themes. Scratchpad f_tbase8_*/f_ta8_*: 70.4%/0.371 to 63.8%/0.606 (n=480), matching; f_tbase4_*/f_ta4_*: 85.2%/0.060 to 82.1%/0.104, matching. quests.js:116 passes no trial flag today.
verdicts.demand: Trigger only at the progress point (half the walk, rescue after freeing), never at the first fight, so the squad meets the garrison at full strength first and the turn is a second act with a visible lead; re-measure. Keep weight 5. Thread trial: false through quests.js:116 as an explicit change. Decide what frail means: either an unturned ward becomes killable (so FAIL.died can fire and the retreat state is honest) or delete the flag. The turn log line states species, grade and offset, not 'is not what the contract said'.

verdicts.attack: The engineering is the cleanest of the pursuit four, but the price is the most overpaid of the twelve at the levels players will meet it: at levels 1-4 the measured change is 85.2% to 82.1% wins and +0.044 deaths per run for x1.5; the terrain lens's rule gives about 1.07-1.09 on those inputs and the arrivals rule about 1.1; only at levels 1-8 (+0.235 deaths) does it approach 1.3. The builder calls 1.5 'generous at low level' and keeps it. weight 5 to 12 triples the row's share and feeds the TWIST_FULL problem. Under guard orders (GUARD_LEASH 2, field.js:49) nearly every first fight has a squad member within 3 tiles of the ward, so the turn is the first fight on 98% of won sorties: the twist is 'the escort's first fight includes an elite Death Knight at level-3', which the tooltip should say in those words. Depends on u-honesty (mods), u-retreat (exitState 'order' after the turn) and the trial threading that quests.js:116 does not have.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: row :833-834; fighterFor returns null without a species :133; resolve() cancels a fight with no fighters on one side :158-161 and sets noFightUntil; frail at :414 and :599 with no reader; escalate rewrites terms :1540-1541 and save() stores mission; ward goal :758-764; combatant() ward branch :1185-1195; makeActor :1662-1688 lines are the ones to copy; ACTOR_KEYS carries role, side, grade, species, hp, maxHp, power, speed, wits, levelOffset; matches() :98 by name keeps 'ward' atoms pointing after the role changes; BESTIARY elite tier is slime_arcane, slime_dark, slime_holy, stone_golem, death_knight and only death_knight carries humanoid or undead, so the Death Knight claim holds for escort (humanoid/beast/goblin) and rescue (humanoid/goblin/undead). Logs reproduce every quoted figure: tbase4 84/85/87% 0.06/0.06/0.07, ta4 80/83/83% 0.11/0.06/0.14, tbase8 68/73/71% 0.50/0.32/0.29, ta8 62/64/65% 0.71/0.58/0.53, grade sweep t_a_vet8 0.49, t_a_lv8 1.11, t_a_e-2 1.04, t_a_e-4 0.71, t_a_e-6 0.59 against t_base_lv8 0.50. Frequencies match my live3-plus-row simulation, not the all-nine pool.
verdicts.demand: Price by level band with the agreed rule (or make the multiplier a function of level like the fee), measured on test/sortie.harness.js. Keep weight near 5-8 until TWIST_FULL is owned. State the mechanism plainly in MOD_TEXT. Sequence after u-honesty and u-retreat and thread trial through roll(). Then it can land as the Turncoat row; retrieval and siege lose the tag.

sharedRules: Shared rules the user approved for every complication: (1) one price rule: the multiplier keeps expected gems per attempt equal, counting a death at PULL_COST (100 gems), R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), rounded up to the next 0.05; (2) every number is re-measured on test/sortie.harness.js (add TWISTS=, GEAR=1 options if missing), not on a private runner; (3) at most one body-adding complication per contract (reinforcements, hunted, trap, turncoat, infested) until pairs are measured; (4) log lines state what spawned, where, at what distance and which term changed, in the engineering register; (5) trial: false on every row that adds bodies, threaded through quests.js.

conflicts: Three pricing conventions for the same quantity. Terrain prices a death at PULL_COST 100 gems and rounds up to 0.05; arrivals prices it at 200 gems plus kill drops; pursuit uses the relative rise in deaths with no formula. Same-sized effects get different multipliers: hunted-a +0.11 deaths per run -> x1.4, reinforcements-a +0.16 -> x1.25, infested-a +0.14 -> x1.50, trap-a +0.012 -> x1.15, storm-a +0.03 -> x1.05. None of the multipliers is derivable by the player from anything on screen (numbers-must-be-traceable); the per-twist record all three propose as the check is specified three ways (gs.field.twists { sent, won, dead } in terrain and arrivals; 'u-ledger can add' in pursuit) and u-ledger part A defines only gs.field.types. One owner, one R stated as data, one record shape.

Exit-route stacking. reinforcements-a (column from the entry 45 s after contact), hunted-a and hunted-b (a body trailing the squad), trap-a (a mark at the way home) and turncoat-a (the ward at the far end) all add bodies to the walk out, where the pursuit lens measured most deaths already occur. rollTwists allows two twists per contract (missiontypes.js:863, max 2) and no proposal measured any pair; the multipliers multiply (1.25 x 1.4 = 1.75) while the deaths very likely compound. Hardcore pairs are treated four different ways (trap-a skips once escalated, reinforcements-a skips arrival groups in the escalation re-spawn, infested-b doubles the escalation re-spawn through the swollen count, storms scale the escape window) and none is measured.

hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same mechanism (a hostile group released behind the squad that reaches it on the way out); the pursuit builder says approve one. hunted-a's dominant effect (the squad bumps into a trailing elite) is the same mechanism again with one body.

Every proposal depends on u-honesty (MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, TWIST_FULL, MT.factors, MT.payout), none of which exists in the code (grep finds no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, TWIST_FULL or MT.current in *.js). The mods fold table would carry about 15 keys with three fold semantics (multiply: move, damage, regen, sight; union/concat: noReach, status, arrivals; largest: promote; sum: swell; first: ambush, pit; plus follower/pack/turn/informant) and the pursuit rows add a cast: (lv) => [...] function on the TWISTS row that must never reach a saved mission. 'A twist is a table row plus one consumer' becomes a dispatch table; the fold rules need one owner and one test.

Field flags for 'a hostile that moves on its own trigger' are named four ways: march (reinforcements-a), stance 'trail' / 'pack' plus follows (hunted-a/b), spotted preset true (hunted), spottedAt (reinforcements-b); each adds ACTOR_KEYS entries and a chooseGoals branch. trapTick/ringTile are claimed by trap-a and trap-b and offered to Reinforcements. u-retreat's contacted() is edited by trap-a (adds s.trapped) and paralleled by reinforcements-a's contactAt; one definition of contact must serve the button, the column clock and the trap.

Frequency figures use different rules: terrain and pursuit quote u-honesty's odds x weight / 66; arrivals quotes today's rule with nine rows. With all rows live the legal pool exceeds 66 on every type (73 to 102 by weights proposed), so the honesty promise 'others unchanged until the weights sum to 66' fails slightly: by my exact two-draw calculation over the 16 types, at level 10 dry falls 6.5% to 5.9-6.1% and hardcore 5.5% to 5.0-5.2%. reinforcements-b (weight 24) and turncoat-a (weight 12) are weight hikes with no stated reason beyond compensating 'only'.

storm-a and storm-b are alternatives, but storm-b's bow rule changes every water-spell Wet outside storms (elements.js:170 is shared with spellcraft.js:54), while storm-a's lives only in combat.js; approving storm-b as written is a global balance change, approving storm-a is a twist-local special case. Both carry the same unpriced walking tax on window contracts.

Three private combat-backed runners (proto/exp/real.js, arrivals/run.js, pursuit/run.js) with three baselines (82.4%/0.10-0.115, 69.5%/0.258, 68.4%/0.251 deaths per run) that cannot be compared, while test/sortie.harness.js, the project's combat-backed harness (named in memory and in test/field.harness.js's header), was used by none; the terrain lens asks for 'a combat-backed runner in test/' that already exists.
missed: Trials. quests.js:116 rolls trial twists through MT.roll with no flag and no filter, so star trials, including the one-body solo road, draw every row. Only the pursuit lens adds trial: false, and it describes quests.js:116 as already passing trial: true, which it does not. Storm, Reinforcements (at least one extra body per written group against a single character), Infested and A trap on a solo trial are unmeasured and unexcluded.

The one-sided-fight quirk. sortie.js:158-160 gives noFightUntil = clock + 120 to every actor in a skirmish whose party or foes list is empty, so any hostile that catches a lone ward (no species, no fighter) is pacified for 120 in-game seconds. trap-a and turncoat-a both put a mark next to a ward, and nobody checked this path; it is also the reason 0 of 960 wards died, which the pursuit lens reports as a fact without the cause.

Phase 'leaving' is set both by withdraw() (field.js:383, a broken squad running) and by leave() (field.js:1875, the job done). The pursuit lens's premise that the walk out is 'the unthreatened part of a run' (76 of 100 deaths after leaving) counts post-withdrawal deaths; u-retreat's exitState reads s.withdrew and s.phase too. Any design that keys on 'the walk home' needs the two split.

The walking-speed term on window contracts. makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308); both storms scale only Hardcore's escape window, so escort and rescue (deadline true -> window) take the whole x0.8 tax: storm-b's own result file shows escort deaths 0.07 to 0.20-0.23 per run, unreported, and storm-a's shows rescue 0.07 to 0.12 from the move term alone.

Loadouts are planned once against a pseudoZone of species at mission level (missions.js:97-100 samples every species at mission.level; sortie.js:112 keys the cache by species count). infested-a's promoted third is fielded at level + 3 but planned against at mission level; storm-a/b and reinforcements-a patch the cache key, infested-a does not. missionProfile needs the fielded level per body or the brilliant-mind planning advantage the storm proposals claim does not exist for promoted casts.

Permadeath value. The user rates anything that prevents a death far above damage; all twelve proposals add deaths (+0.012 to +0.235 per run) and none adds a lever that prevents one. The only readable 'leave now' signals are reinforcements-a's countdown and hunted-a's HP gate. A complication whose counterplay is a death-prevention action (a window in which the retreat order is free again, a spotter kill that cancels an arrival the squad can see) would fit the stated values; none was proposed.

Register. Proposed log lines include 'The paper was wrong: <label> is here for them', 'The floor gives way', 'the pack closes in', 'come out of the dark', 'The informant left': narrative, not the mechanic and the number (ui-prose-engineer-style). Every new line should read like the existing 'Complications: Storm' and 'wave 2 of 4' lines: what spawned, where, at what distance, and which term changed.

Save compatibility of board offers. A held board offer or saved run rolled before the build carries a twist id whose row now has mods or a cast function; the pursuit lens stales such offers through MT.current, the arrivals lens does not (a saved 'reinforcements' contract pays x1.25 with no column until the board rerolls), and the terrain lens derives mods from mission.twists so old runs change behaviour mid-run on reload. One rule for 'an offer rolled under an older table' is needed across all rows.

No proposal measured on a real save with gear and potions (all say so) or with the two-twist pairs the board can roll; and no proposal gives the overseer a repeatable command in test/ that reproduces its headline numbers, which test/sortie.harness.js's OUT/diff mode already supports.

conflicts: Alternatives on one row: storm-a/storm-b, trap-a/trap-b, reinforcements-a/reinforcements-b, infested-a/infested-b, hunted-a/hunted-b each re-add the same TWISTS id with different mods keys, MOD_TEXT lines, weights and only/not lists; at most one per row can land, and the arrivals lens did not say so for its two pairs.

Three incompatible price rules. Terrain: R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x PULL_COST(100) / (p1 x W0), no drops. Arrivals: m = (W0 F0 + L0 + 200 dd - L1) / (W1 F1), a death costs 200 and kill drops count. Pursuit: the measured relative rise in deaths, no formula. On the same inputs hunted-a is 1.19 (terrain rule), 1.24 (arrivals rule) or 1.4 (as proposed); turncoat-a at levels 1-4 is about 1.08 against 1.5; infested-a is 1.31 against 1.50; storm-a is 1.05 against about 1.10. u-honesty's MT.factors prints these multipliers side by side on one card, so the six rows must be priced by one rule.

Weight budget. u-honesty's draw rule is odds x min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL) with TWIST_FULL = 66 and the promise that adding rows leaves the others unchanged 'until the weights sum to 66'. The original nine rows sum to 84; with the A variants the per-type pool is 75-87, with the B variants 64-96 (reinforcements-b 24, infested-b 13, turncoat-a 12), so the cap binds everywhere: my simulation (60000 rolls per level) has night 7.89% to 7.51%, dry 6.49% to 6.02%, hardcore 5.67% to 5.19% at level 10 under the A weights, and each lens computed its own frequency under a different pool (pursuit: three live rows plus its own; terrain: the same; arrivals: all nine on the current rule). One owner must set TWIST_FULL to the real total or rescale the weights.

Four cue-spawn mechanisms for one idea. reinforcements-a/b: cast groups with arrive {on, delay} and a fired flag in map.spawns, march stance, contactAt/spottedAt; hunted-a/b: TEMPORAL 'trail', cued(), counters.trailed, stance trail/pack with their own chooseGoals branches and taskGoal/rally skips; trap-a: springAmbush with ringTile and a mark; all walk a new hostile group onto the map on a cue and give it a goal rule. The axes memory asks for one mechanism with data ({on, delay, from, stance}) read by one spawner and one goal branch; the pursuit lens itself says the stance code 'should land once'.
hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same effect (bodies arriving from the entry behind the squad) under two labels and two prices (x1.4 and x1.25); the pursuit lens says do not approve both.

Trial roads. hunted-a/b and turncoat-a/b add trial: false and a rollTwists filter; storm, trap, reinforcements and infested do not, so a one-body solo trial can roll Reinforcements, Infested or Storm. The claim that quests.js:116 passes trial: true is false today (mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option), so whichever lands first must thread it.

u-retreat's contacted() is extended three ways: trap-a adds !!s.trapped, reinforcements-a mirrors it with s.contactAt set in look() and openSkirmish(), hunted pre-marks followers spotted to stay out of it; one definition of contact, in one place, before any of these.

MOD_TEXT shape. u-honesty specifies a static table keyed by mod; terrain and arrivals generate per-contract text (member lines, 'x bodies on this paper', species tags), so the honesty API must take (mods, mission) before these build; infested-b's and reinforcements-a's cards cannot be produced from the static table.

All three lenses say wave 1 is editing field.js, sortie.js, combat.js and missiontypes.js. Wave 1 is finished (.team-backup/r1w1, project files dated 01:xx-03:06); wave 2 started at 03:09 (.team-backup/r1w2) and holds u-honesty, u-retreat, u-wounds, u-ledger, u-readout and u-debrief, which touch every file these twelve cite. Every line number here moves before any of them builds, and none lists after: ['u-honesty', 'u-retreat'] in a form the scheduler reads.
missed: u-honesty is approved but not built: missiontypes.js has no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, MT.factors or TWIST_FULL (grep across *.js is empty) and its spec moves the six rows out of TWISTS into a comment block. All twelve proposals write MODS entries against that API and re-add rows it removes; none states the dependency as a build order, and a builder landing before it would write a second, incompatible fold.

None of the three lenses used test/sortie.harness.js (u-harness, approved and present: boots game.html's script list through test/game.boot.js and plays real Sortie launch/skip/settle with combat.js, gear, potions, Condition pools and Outfit). Each wrote a private runner that re-implements resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast with gearless parties; every absolute death rate is an upper bound by the builders' own admission, and every multiplier is priced on those numbers. The field-balance-harness memory says to quote game figures from sortie.harness.js.

Storm and the window clock: escort, assassination, rescue, pursuit, sabotage and capture carry deadline: true (missiontypes.js:409, :524, :595, :618, :640, :708), exitFor (:195) gives them the window exit, and shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1313). Walking x0.8 shortens the usable window by 20% on six types; neither storm design scales or discloses it (only Hardcore's escalate seconds are scaled).

escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch (:1373-1376) respawn 50% / 30% of every hostile and patrol spawn group with no check for deferred, at, arrive or follows, so any twist that adds a cast group gets it cloned on escalation and on every window shut. reinforcements-a skips its groups; hunted-a and hunted-b do not.

Stale offers: boards re-roll every 6 minutes (sortie.js:97) but trial offers persist per character until the star changes (quests.js:112); any twist that changes the cast at roll time (reinforcements-a/b, infested-a/b, hunted-a/b) leaves already-rolled offers carrying the tag with no bodies behind it and the multiplier still applied. Only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check.

describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast; the card's hostile figure includes a column or follower unless excluded. hunted-a excludes follows groups; reinforcements-a/b do not.

combat.js types a spell's main strike by strikes[0].type (:303) and its splash as 'arcane' (:308); storm-a's per-type damage multiplier misses heat splash. Riposte (:215) uses the target's damageType and DoT (:593) the condition's type, so those paths are covered.

trap-a sets s.doneAt = null at the spring; verdict() (field.js:1636) withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (2.5), so a late squad is pulled out at the moment the ambush appears.

The measured cost of hunted-a, hunted-b and part of reinforcements-a is a body on the route home (hunted-a: 49 of 52 follower-fight deaths after leaving; hunted-b: 84 of 86; reinforcements-a: 26% of firings after the walk home starts), while the tooltips describe triggers (HP under 70%, commit at 60%, contact + 45 s) that the builders' own sensitivity tables show barely move the outcome. Under the traceable-numbers rule the card has to name the thing that costs.

Positive levelOffset is new to the engine: SWARMED (field.js:84) clamps it to 0.15 and feeds makeActor hp/power (:1682-1683) and every odds() call tactics makes; infested-a includes the fix, but nothing else that reads levelOffset was audited for the sign (bestiary brief, noteSighting and castLevel add it correctly; the plain harness and tactics tests assume it is negative).

Perf was measured for one proposal only (infested-b: hostiles per run 13 to 24, 35 at level 8, Node only). turncoat-b puts an actor scan under found()/known() (10 call sites in field.js, several inside per-actor filters per step); trap-b rebuilds the map mid-run; reinforcements-b scans the whole tile grid once per call. None was timed in the browser.

Evidence slips that do not change verdicts but should be corrected in the specs: terrain's fire-word class list (classes.js has mastery 'fire' in grenadier :466, artillerist :566 and kineticist :999, not arcanist or elemental_mage; the picker line must come from Classes.lexiconOf at classes.js:1818, which the proposal does name); pursuit's 'quests.js:116 passes trial: true' (it passes level and name only); the 1950-run storm figures and all trap figures are not in any results file in the scratchpad (proto/out holds storm_random.txt at n=1500 with different death rates, storm_b_wet.txt and storm_b_cands.txt), while every pursuit log and the arrivals final-n100 files reproduce the quoted numbers.
